metadata.title:
Morgondagens medborgare
ICCS 2009: svenska 14-åringars kunskaper, värderingar och deltagande i internationell belysning

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2009 used a two-stage sampling design with representative schools and selected intact classes in grade 8, with an additional national oversample for grade 9 and for specific school types/contexts (e.g., schools with high shares of students with foreign background). The report states that data were weighted to allow generalization to the grade-8 target population, and it also describes a rotated design for the achievement test (students receive different subsets of items). However, the manuscript does not name the specific student weight variable(s) (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) nor does it describe replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because this is a descriptive large-scale assessment report (not an ML modeling paper), the appropriate weighting guidance is to use the ICCS-provided sampling weights in the international database when producing population-representative estimates and to apply the test-design aggregation method for the rotated test.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report is primarily a descriptive and comparative analysis of ICCS outcomes (knowledge scales, attitude/value scales, and participation indices) rather than an empirical predictive modeling study that explicitly documents plausible-value (PV) generation/combination and missing-data handling at the student level. ICCS uses scaled scores and indices derived from test and questionnaire responses; the report does not provide a PV-specific methodological section (e.g., Rubin combining rules) nor a missing-data strategy (e.g., listwise/pairwise deletion or imputation). Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported in the level of detail required for extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target population is students in grade 8 in ICCS 2009, with a national additional sample including grade 9 students for Sweden. The report states that in Sweden 3,464 students in grade 8 and 3,515 students in grade 9 participated on 169 schools. The sampling was two-stage: representative schools were selected first, then one (in some cases two) intact class(es) in grade 8 per school. The report also notes exclusions from the sampling frame for certain school types (e.g., special schools and schools not following the Swedish curriculum) and that some students were excluded by school coordinators (e.g., certain physical disabilities, intellectual disability, and newly arrived students), with an overall exclusion share reported.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 assessed Swedish 14-year-olds (grade 8, with an additional grade 9 sample in Sweden) in 38 participating “countries/regions” using a rotated test design and multiple questionnaires. The knowledge test covered two cognitive domains (knowing; reasoning and analyzing) and four content areas (society/political systems, fundamental values, civic participation, civic identities), with results reported on a standardized scale (international mean fixed at 500, SD 100). The report finds that Swedish students score significantly above the international mean (537 vs. 500) and above the European mean (514), with Finland, Denmark, South Korea, and Taiwan scoring significantly higher than Sweden. Equity-related analyses show larger within-student variation in Sweden than the European average, relatively low between-class variation, and substantial associations between parental education (socioeconomic background) and knowledge outcomes. Methodologically, the report is descriptive/comparative and does not present an ML predictive pipeline; it also does not document PV combination or missing-data handling procedures in extractable detail.
